# Ghoti: full documentation

> Ghoti is a single-binary, in-memory server for coordination primitives. It gives a fleet of services up to 1,000 configurable slots (token-bucket and leaky-bucket rate limiters, timeout-memory leases, atomic counters, tickers, simple memory, broadcast and multicast channels) over a plain-text TCP protocol (`standard` or `telnet`) or HTTP with Server-Sent Events. No client library is required.

Key facts:

- All state is in memory. A restart empties every slot; nothing is persisted.
- Values are opaque byte strings of at most 36 bytes; requests are 4 to 40 bytes; one request in flight per connection.
- Commands: `r<slot>` read, `w<slot><value>` write, `s<slot>`/`d<slot>` subscribe/leave (multicast), `u`/`p` login, `q` quit. Responses start with `v` (value), `e` (error, `e<slot><code>`) or `a` (async event).
- Start the server with `ghoti run`; it reads `config.yaml` from `/etc/ghoti`, `$HOME/.ghoti` or the current directory and exits if none is found. Default address `localhost:9090`.
- No TLS on any listener. Broadcast/multicast delivery is at most once. Clustering (leader election, no replication) is experimental.
- Latest release: v0.3.0. License: Apache-2.0. Source: https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti

Generated from https://ghoti.miocevic.com/ on 2026-11-21. Each section below is one page of the site; its URL is given under the title.


---

# Overview

URL: https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/

Ghoti is a single-binary, in-memory server for small pieces of shared state that a fleet of services needs to agree on: a rate limit, a lease, a counter, a signal.  [**Getting started →**Install, verify, first run.](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/getting-started/) [**Protocol →**Commands, framing, retries.](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/) [**Slot reference →**Every slot kind and its options.](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/) [**Error codes →**What each `e` response means.](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/reference/errors/)

## What Ghoti is

A Ghoti server exposes 1000 numbered **slots**, `000` to `999`. You decide in `config.yaml` which slots exist and what kind each one is. Clients read and write slots with a plain-text protocol over TCP, or over HTTP. Each slot kind has a fixed behaviour:

| Kind | What it does | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [`simple_memory`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#simple-memory) | Holds a value of up to 36 bytes. | Implemented |
| [`timeout_memory`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#timeout-memory) | A value with an owner: only the connection that last wrote it can write again, until the owner's timeout expires. | Implemented |
| [`token_bucket`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#token-bucket) | Hands out tokens refilled every period. | Implemented |
| [`leaky_bucket`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#leaky-bucket) | Accepts a request if the bucket has room, leaking one token every `refresh_rate` ms. | Implemented |
| [`ticker`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#ticker) | An integer that counts down by one every `refresh_rate` ms until it reaches zero. | Implemented |
| [`atomic`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#atomic) | A counter that increments on every read. | Implemented |
| [`broadcast`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#broadcast) | A write is pushed to every connected client. | Implemented |
| [`multicast`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/#multicast) | A write is pushed to the clients that subscribed to the slot. | Implemented |
| Random signal propagation | A write delivered to one subscriber chosen at random. | Planned |

Around the slots Ghoti has:

- Three transports: `standard` TCP (the default), `telnet`, and `http` with Server-Sent Events for broadcast slots. See [Transports](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/transports/).
- Optional users with per-slot read and write permissions. See [Authentication](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/authentication/).
- An optional Prometheus endpoint and a connection cap. See [Operations](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/operations/).
- Leader election between several nodes, without replication. Experimental See [Cluster](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/cluster/).

## What Ghoti is not

- **Not a database or a durable store.** Nothing is written to disk. A restart empties every slot, and a newly elected cluster leader starts empty.
- **Not a message queue.** Broadcast and multicast deliver at most once, with no retries and no backlog for clients that were not connected.
- **Not encrypted.** No listener supports TLS, and the `p` login command sends the password in cleartext. Terminate TLS in a load balancer or reverse proxy, or keep traffic on a trusted network. See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- **Not a consensus system.** Clustering elects a leader with the bully algorithm. There is no quorum and no replication, and split-brain is possible under network partitions.

## Guarantees at a glance

| Topic | What Ghoti does |
|---|---|
| Durability | None. All state is in memory and is lost on restart. |
| Ordering on one connection | Responses come back in the order the commands were sent. Async events never appear in the middle of a response. |
| Ordering across connections | No guarantee. |
| Requests in flight | One per connection. Send a command, wait for its response, then send the next. |
| Event delivery | At most once. One attempt per client and no retries. The writer receives a `received/sent/errors` summary. |
| Lease ownership | Tied to the TCP connection. It survives a dropped connection until the timeout expires and is forgotten on restart. |
| Values | Opaque byte strings of at most 36 bytes, returned exactly as written. |
| Transport security | None built in. Bring your own TLS termination. |
| High availability | Experimental Leader election only. Followers answer `NOT_LEADER` and do not redirect. |

## Performance

On a 2-core, 1 GiB AWS t4g.micro, Ghoti v0.3.0 answered with a 0.29 ms median round trip on one connection, served over 127,000 requests per second with 100 connections, and spent 7.6 µs on average inside the server per memory read. See [Benchmarks](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/benchmarks/) for the method, every result and how to reproduce them.

## When it fits

Ghoti fits state that is cheap to lose and expensive to coordinate: a fleet-wide rate limit, a lease that picks one active worker, a counter for distinct numbers, or a push signal such as "reload the configuration". If the overall system must keep working when Ghoti is down, possibly degraded, Ghoti is a good fit. If losing the data is not acceptable, use a durable store instead.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Ghoti persist data?

No. All state is in memory and nothing is written to disk. A restart empties every slot, and a newly elected cluster leader starts empty. Use Ghoti for state that is cheap to lose and expensive to coordinate.

### Is Ghoti a replacement for Redis?

Not as a general-purpose store. Ghoti has a fixed set of slot kinds, values of at most 36 bytes, no persistence and no data structures to query. It covers coordination primitives (rate limits, leases, counters and fan-out signals) with a one-line text protocol and a single binary.

### Does Ghoti support TLS?

No. No listener implements TLS, and the login password and HTTP Basic Auth credentials travel in cleartext. Terminate TLS in a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of Ghoti, or keep the traffic on a trusted network.

### What happens to a lease when the client disconnects or the server restarts?

A lease on a `timeout_memory` slot belongs to the TCP connection. If the client disconnects, the lease stays held until its timeout expires, and a reconnecting client is a new owner that gets error 007 until then. If Ghoti restarts, the lease is forgotten and the first connection to write takes it, so two clients can briefly both believe they hold it.

### Are broadcast and multicast messages guaranteed to arrive?

No. Delivery is at most once: one attempt per client, no retries and no replay for clients that were not connected. The writer receives a received/sent/errors count for each message.

### Which languages and clients can use Ghoti?

Any language that can open a TCP socket and send a line of text. There is no client library to install. Over the HTTP transport, slots are read and written with GET and POST, and browsers can receive broadcast events with Server-Sent Events. For manual testing, nc is enough.

### How fast is Ghoti?

In the v0.3.0 benchmark on a 2-vCPU, 1-GiB AWS t4g.micro, Ghoti served 134,343 memory reads per second at a 0.60 ms median round trip with 100 connections, and answered in 0.29 ms at the median with one connection, network included. The method and every result are on the [Benchmarks](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/benchmarks/) page.

### Can Ghoti run as a cluster?

Experimentally. Nodes elect a leader with the bully algorithm, but there is no replication and no quorum, and split-brain is possible under network partitions. Followers answer with a NOT_LEADER error naming the leader instead of redirecting the client.

### How many slots are there, and how large can values be?

There are 1,000 slots, numbered 000 to 999, each defined in config.yaml. A value is an opaque byte string of at most 36 bytes, and a request is 4 to 40 bytes long.


---

# Getting started

URL: https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/getting-started/

Four commands to a working server: install, write a configuration, start it, and talk to it with `nc`. Install options, download verification and troubleshooting come after.

## Quick start

**1. Install.** With Go installed (the version in [`go.mod`](https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/blob/main/go.mod)), this puts `ghoti` in `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`. Without Go, use a [release archive](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/getting-started/#from-a-release-archive).

```sh
$ go install github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/cmd/ghoti@latest
```

**2. Declare two slots**, a value and a counter, in a `config.yaml` in an empty directory:

```sh
$ mkdir ghoti-demo && cd ghoti-demo
$ printf 'slot_000:\n  kind: simple_memory\nslot_001:\n  kind: atomic\n' > config.yaml
```

**3. Start the server** from that directory. It listens on `localhost:9090`:

```sh
$ ghoti run
time=2026-11-20T06:48:59.858Z level=INFO msg="Starting server..."
```

**4. Talk to it** from a second terminal. Run `nc localhost 9090` and type one command per line. Lines starting with `>` are what you type, and lines starting with `<` are the server's answers:

```text
> w000hello
< v000hello
> r000
< v000hello
> r001
< v0011
> r001
< v0012
> r002
< e002005
> x000
< exxx001
```

- `w000hello` writes `hello` to slot 000, and the server echoes the stored value.
- Each read of the atomic slot 001 increments it.
- Slot 002 is not configured, so the answer is error [`005`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/reference/errors/#error-005) (MISSING_SLOT).
- `x` is not a command, so the answer is [`001`](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/reference/errors/#error-001) (PARSE_ERROR), with `xxx` in place of the slot number.

Send `q` to close the connection, and stop the server with `Ctrl`+`C`. Something different? See [Troubleshooting](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/getting-started/#troubleshooting).

## Install options

### From a release archive

Every release on the [releases page](https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/releases) has one archive per platform. The archive has the `ghoti` binary at its root, together with the README, the license and the changelog.

| Platform | Archive |
|---|---|
| Linux (`amd64`, `arm64`, `386`) | `ghoti_<version>_linux_<arch>.tar.gz` |
| macOS (`amd64`, `arm64`) | `ghoti_<version>_darwin_<arch>.tar.gz` |
| Windows (`amd64`, `386`) | `ghoti_<version>_windows_<arch>.zip` |

Set `VERSION` to the release you want, without the leading `v`. The latest release is 0.3.0.

```sh
$ VERSION=0.3.0
$ curl -LO "https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/releases/download/v${VERSION}/ghoti_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
$ tar -xzf "ghoti_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz"
$ ./ghoti version
```

### With `go install`

Building from source needs the Go version listed in [`go.mod`](https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/blob/main/go.mod). The binary is installed into `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`, which must be on your `PATH`.

```sh
$ go install github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/cmd/ghoti@latest
```

## Verifying a download

Each release also ships:

- A `checksums.txt` file with the SHA-256 of every archive.
- A Sigstore signature of the checksums file, `checksums.txt.sigstore.json`.
- An SPDX SBOM next to every archive, `<archive>.sbom.json`.
- A build provenance attestation for every archive.

Together they let you check that what you downloaded is what the Release workflow built from the tag.

### Checksum

The checksum catches a corrupted or tampered download:

```sh
$ curl -LO "https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt"
$ sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
```

### Signature

The signature proves that `checksums.txt` itself was produced by this repository's Release workflow. It is a keyless [Sigstore](https://www.sigstore.dev/) signature, so you check it against the workflow identity rather than against a key you have to trust. The signature, the certificate and the transparency log entry come together in one bundle file. The check needs [cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) v3:

```sh
$ curl -LO "https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/releases/download/v${VERSION}/checksums.txt.sigstore.json"
$ cosign verify-blob \
    --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
    --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v' \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
    checksums.txt
```

### Provenance

The provenance attestation ties an archive to the exact commit and workflow run that built it. You check it with the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/), and it doesn't need any other file:

```sh
$ gh attestation verify "ghoti_${VERSION}_linux_amd64.tar.gz" --repo dankomiocevic/ghoti
```

The SBOM lists the Go modules linked into the binary, for scanners like [grype](https://github.com/anchore/grype) or for your own inventory.

## Troubleshooting

### The server exits with `Config File "config" Not Found`

Ghoti needs a configuration file. It looks for `config.yaml` in `/etc/ghoti`, then `$HOME/.ghoti`, then the current directory. **If it finds none, it exits with status 1** rather than starting with defaults:

```sh
$ cd /tmp/demo && ghoti run
2026/11/20 06:49:31 ERROR Error loading config error="failed to load server config: Config File \"config\" Not Found in \"[/etc/ghoti /home/demo/.ghoti /tmp/demo]\""
$ echo $?
1
```

Run `ghoti run` from the directory that holds `config.yaml`, or put the file in one of the other two locations.

### Every command answers `exxx001`

You are probably connected with `telnet`. The default `standard` transport ends requests with a bare `\n`, but a telnet client sends `\r\n`, so reads fail with `exxx001` and written values keep a trailing `\r`. Use `nc`, or set `protocol: telnet` in the configuration. See [Transports](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/transports/).

### A slot you configured answers `e<slot>005`

Its definition is invalid, for example an unknown `kind` or a missing required option, and the server skipped it without a warning. Check the slot against the [slot reference](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/).

## Next steps

- [Walk through coordination with two clients](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/blog/2025/07/25/implementing-leader-election-with-ghoti/): build leader election on a lease slot.
- Read [Concepts](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/concepts/) for how slots, connections and ownership behave.
- Pick slot kinds for your problem in the [slot reference](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/).
- Learn the exact rules your client must follow in [Protocol](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/).
